Best telescopes under $500

Every scope here costs under $500 — ranked from cheapest to priciest, because I know that’s how you’re reading it. This is the sweet spot for a first telescope: enough aperture for Saturn’s rings and real deep-sky objects, without the regret if you upgrade later. (You probably will. We all do.)

#1

Celestron AstroMaster 70AZ around $150

The honest $150 start. A real refractor with zero collimation fuss — lovely on the Moon and planets, and cheap enough that it doesn't matter if the hobby doesn't stick.

The honest $150 start. No shame in starting here.

  • Watch out:
  • 70mm limits deep-sky views
  • Basic mount is wobbly at high power
Read the full pick →

#2

Orion StarBlast 4.5 Astro Reflector around $250

The tabletop Dobsonian classic. More sky per dollar than cheap refractors — though you’ll need to put it on something sturdy, like the world’s most exciting side table.

On a table, observing in 60 seconds. Try the hobby on for size.

  • Watch out:
  • Needs a sturdy table
  • Fast f/4 mirror needs collimation
Read the full pick →

#3

Sky-Watcher Evostar 102 around $280

A sharp 4-inch refractor — but heads up, it’s the tube only, so save room in the budget for a mount and tripod.

Old-school refractor. Razor-sharp Moon, zero maintenance.

  • Watch out:
  • Optical tube only — needs a mount and tripod
  • Achromatic design shows false color on bright objects
Read the full pick →

#4

Sky-Watcher Heritage 150P around $300

My sweet-spot pick, and I’ll defend it at family dinner: 6 inches of Dobsonian showing Saturn’s rings, Jupiter’s bands, and hundreds of deep-sky objects.

Six inches of 'oh wow' that fits on a camping table.

  • Watch out:
  • Needs a sturdy table or stool
  • No tracking — planets drift
Read the full pick →

#5

Orion SkyQuest XT6 around $450

The full-size 6-inch Dobsonian — the one that’s been making beginners happy for decades. Classics are classics for a reason.

The 6-inch Dobsonian that raised a generation of stargazers.

  • Watch out:
  • Long tube needs car transport
  • No tracking
Read the full pick →

#6

Celestron StarSense Explorer DX 130AZ around $480

Your phone guides you to 100+ targets — training wheels that actually teach you the constellations instead of doing your homework for you.

Your phone teaches you the sky while you observe.

  • Watch out:
  • Phone mount adds fiddliness
  • 130mm won't resolve fine planetary detail
Read the full pick →
